result:
Both PRs are `MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN`. Final state:

- **PR #11** (https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/11) — carries the actual fix: `worker-entrypoint.sh`'s genuine no-op branch now checkpoints `pending_review` and starts the supervisor instead of checkpointing `completed` directly (which the live `veridian-task.py` guard was silently rejecting). Also adds `tests/worker_noop_pending_review_test.sh`.
- **PR #20** (https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/20) — this task's `PROGRESS.md` log, mirroring the earlier PR #19 precedent.
- The live production file `/opt/veridian/scripts/worker-entrypoint.sh` was also patched directly so the actual running system is fixed, not just tracked source.

Verified with two independent real reproductions (not just code reading): a shell-level test that extracts and evals the actual shipped bash block under a real git fixture (fails on old code, passes on new), and a Python-level reproduction driving the real, unmodified `veridian-task.py` checkpoint guard through a fake task's lifecycle, confirming the old path silently gets rejected (task stuck at `in_progress`) while the new path succeeds.

I chose routing through `pending_review` over inventing a new terminal status (e.g. `completed_no_changes`) because several other scripts (sync-controller-back.py, queue-dispatcher.py, health-check-15min.py) hardcode which statuses are "terminal" — a new unrecognized status would reproduce the same stuck-task bug under a different name, and fixing those was out of this task's scope.
